    The walk construction and Theorem 5.2 #

    Alternative (3) of Theorem 3.14 in data form. Walk.WalkData k A consists of a presentation π : kQ → A (a surjective algebra homomorphism) and a primitive walk, given by its cycle D_w and the map p : D_w → Q satisfying (3.4), such that p_*L(T) (Construction 3.12) is an A-module for every T ∈ D_fin. By Lemma 3.13 this holds for every T ∈ D (PushDown.kills_of_fin). The data give push-down data (PushDown.PdData): the classes of block positions are the components of the matching quiver (Lemma 4.7), and a morphism φ with L(φ) vanishing at a vertex is zero by Lemma 2.2(1). The cycle is used in the form dual to Setting 3.11, with a sink; then the facts about S₋ used in Theorem 5.2 hold automatically (WalkData.toPdDatum), so walk data alone give the data of Theorem 5.2.
